title: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years
oneLiner: Most current east-coast production is already contracted; the reserve bites only on new supply.
body: The announced scheme preserves foundation contracts and any signed before the December 2025 cut-off. Since the three Queensland ventures sold most of their output under long-term contracts years ago, the gas actually subject to reservation is a thin slice of new and uncontracted supply, which critics say is too small to shift the domestic price before the 2030s.
contextBackground: This is where the reservation debate now sits. Producers wanted only new gas included and largely got it; the Greens say the policy was written by the industry; the government says a 'modest' oversupply is enough. The September 2026 softening, which pegs the reserve to about 110 per cent of forecast demand, sharpened the question.
contextDisagreement: Supporters of the design say that at the margin even a modest oversupply sets the price, and point to modelling that extra Queensland supply lowers southern prices. Critics say that with Santos the only major venture not already supplying the domestic market, the scheme mostly formalises what two of three producers already do.

otherClaim.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices

claimItself.title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
claimItself.oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
claimItself.body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.

otherClaim.title: In September 2026 the reservation was recast to about 110 per cent of forecast domestic demand, and Santos is the only major east-coast producer not already supplying the domestic market

claimItself.title: In September 2026 the reservation was recast to about 110 per cent of forecast domestic demand, and Santos is the only major east-coast producer not already supplying the domestic market
claimItself.oneLiner: The softened rule reserves little beyond what two of the three ventures already sell locally.
claimItself.body: Reuters reported that the government revised the scheme from a flat 20 per cent of export volumes to a reserve of roughly 110 per cent of estimated domestic demand. Industry welcomed the change while warning that oversupply could depress prices and deter new development. Of the three Queensland ventures, only Santos's GLNG does not supply significant volumes domestically.

otherClaim.title: Modelling cited in support of the scheme found that additional Queensland supply would lower wholesale prices in New South Wales and Victoria

claimItself.title: Modelling cited in support of the scheme found that additional Queensland supply would lower wholesale prices in New South Wales and Victoria
claimItself.oneLiner: The government's 'modest oversupply' claim rests on this kind of result.
claimItself.body: An Energy Edge study cited by The Conversation found that extra gas from Queensland flowing south would reduce prices in the southern states, where the Bass Strait decline is sharpest. The government expects the reservation to create a modest domestic oversupply with the same effect.
